newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria begins 1997 draft budget discussions.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria begins 1997 draft budget discussions.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet on Monday began discussing next year's budget which it says should be balanced between revenue and expenditure if parliament decides to introduce a currency board to stabilise the economy.
"The cabinet will discuss two versions of state expenditure and revenue, one of which involves the introduction of a currency board," a government press officer told reporters.
The government announced last week that it had accepted the International Monetary Fund's proposal for a currency board, which would introduce a fixed exchange rate.
The currency board system, whose adoption must be approved by parliament, halts central bank lending to the government, state enterprises and commercial banks.

Prime Minister Zhan Videnov said last week that the currency board would be implemented early next year after parliament passed a balanced 1997 budget and a package of bank law amendments that would make the plan operational.

An earlier preliminary draft prepared by the finance ministry envisaged a budget deficit of 370 billion levs or nine percent of gross domestic product (GDP), which is estimated at 4.054 trillion levs.

Expenditure was assumed at 1.46 trillion levs and revenue at 1.090 trillion levs. GDP, which fell by 6.2 percent for the first half of this year, was seen falling a further 8.2 percent. The cabinet is expected to continue closed door discussions on the budget throughout the week.
An IMF mission is expected to arrive in Sofia this month to work out the technical details of the currency board plan.
